framing: The crossing formula b=log10(N1/N2)/dM is the classical Utsu two-threshold count estimator, cited as classical. The FINDING is the reduction: the corrected b_op objective / (b-independent M>=3.0 slope) cancels the cascade and equals it, so the sweep carries no information beyond the catalogue's own counts.

A_estimator_agreement.note: if True this is reported as a finding; no tuning of delta or threshold is applied

B_not_averaged: nested samples; quoted as mutually consistent, not averaged. pairwise gaps within ~1-2 binomial sigma.

C_reference_band.note: a labelled reference band inside the b-ensemble range [0.13%, 3.74%]; NOT a second central

FINDING_above_pile.CORRECTED: This supersedes an earlier draft of this block that overclaimed a clean b=1.20 and b_op vindication. Full verification (r20 battery, TEST 1-8) gives the nuanced truth below.
FINDING_above_pile.pile_is_a_conversion_comb: non-cumulative density (TEST7) shows magnitudes quantized onto a grid, alternating ~2000/0 per 0.05 bin, densest 3.3-3.65, thinning above 3.7. mag_w[3.5,4.0) is 68% Md; mag_w[4.0,4.5) is 78% ML. 3.5 is inside the comb.
FINDING_above_pile.wide_interval_reason: only 12 events M>=5.5 and 1 at M>=6; the large-event count cannot pin b above the pile tighter than ~±0.15
FINDING_above_pile.deconfounded_1.40_position: at the UPPER EDGE of the above-pile CI (1.40 vs CI top 1.40); not decisively separated
FINDING_above_pile.anchor_sweep_causation: the count estimate peaks at 3.4->4.5 (1.51, comb edge) and falls to 1.15-1.22 above 4.0; the deconfounded triple anchored at 3.0/3.5 is mildly inflated by the comb
FINDING_above_pile.CONCLUSION: The magnitude law above the pile is b~1.2 but POORLY CONSTRAINED [1.11,1.40]. Both the operational b_op=1.15 and the deconfounded 1.40 lie within this interval; the data cannot choose. This corrects Amendment 7 (which called 1.40 "the magnitude law above the artifact" -- overconfident; it is the upper edge) AND corrects the first draft of this finding (which called b_op vindicated at a clean 1.20 -- also overconfident). P(M>=6) is correspondingly uncertain: b=1.11->~2.5%, b=1.24->~1.1%, b=1.40->0.30%. No single central (neither 1.54%% nor 0.30%%) is defensible; the ensemble range IS the result.

check1_provenance_forking_paths.anchor_choice: M>=4.0 was chosen on the COMB DIAGNOSTIC (magnitude-grid density collapses above 3.7; TEST7), NOT on the resulting b. This pre-empts the forking-paths objection.

SETTLED_b_story.check2_mislabel_fixed: 1.40 is the DECONFOUNDED estimate, not the count-calibration value (the corrected count-calibration returned 1.00/1.05, unidentified). Correct phrasing: the interval spans the operational convention (1.15) and the deconfounded estimate (1.40).
SETTLED_b_story.check3_nonstationarity_caveat: S10.4 pre/post-Kumburgaz slope change (1.30 pre -> 1.14 post) sits INSIDE [1.11,1.40]; the above-pile interval covers a moving target, not a stationary constant.

inner_above_pile_identified.meaning: best-supported statement: the large-event law and its P(M6), directly identified above the comb.
inner_above_pile_identified.do_not_quote_a_central: the band [0.30%, 2.24%] IS the product; quoting ~1.1-1.3% as a central recreates the single-number problem one level up. b_op=1.15 gives 1.5-1.7% inside the band -- that is the continuity-arm value, not a central of the band.

outer_b_ensemble_envelope.meaning: sensitivity envelope covering tail non-GR behaviour and the n=1 M6; retained.

ensemble_endpoints_outside_above_pile.why: they measure the MIXED catalogue (comb-dominated below 4.0), not the large-event law.

GPT critique #4 ("retaining 1.15 looks arbitrary") dissolves: 1.15 is now retrospectively ADMISSIBLE on an identified interval -- admissible, NOT validated (it was not selected by this interval; it happens to fall inside it).
